findings.title: Node restore does not capture or restore the task's own counters (WashLettuce.washed_time, RinseSinkBasin.washed_loc, ScrubCuttingBoard.board_contact_*), so each branch inherits the previous branch's success progress
findings.where: runs/scripts/hidden_state.py:52-60 (py_state: fixtures only), 80-117 (capture/restore); runs/scripts/atomic_eval.py:84-97 (restore_node); runs/20261026_imagine/imagine.py:32-36,75; runs/20261029_closedloop/closedloop.py:57,66,77,88; runs/20261026_critic_data/collect.py:155; official counters: composite/making_salads/wash_lettuce.py:57-63, cleaning_sink/rinse_sink_basin.py:125-136, sanitizing_cutting_board/scrub_cutting_board.py:172-215
findings.description: The final stage of these three tasks is _check_success(), and it reads task-level Python attributes that live on the env, not on a fixture and not in the sim state. py_state() copies only fixtures that override update_state, and capture()/restore() copy controllers, observables and warm start. No restore path (restore_node, imagine.candidate, the closed loop, collect.py) ever resets washed_time, washed_loc, board_contact_positions, board_contact_timer or sponge_contact_height. A candidate rollout from a node therefore starts with whatever the previous candidate left behind. A branch that already rinsed, washed or scrubbed makes every later branch from an earlier node count as an official success. In addition, oracle.set_state runs env.update_state(), so WashLettuce.washed_time is incremented once on every restore while the lettuce is under running water. The sim-state equality guards (collect.py:160-167, closedloop.py:80-82) cannot catch this, because the sim state is identical. Fix 7 (restore_node) covers fixture flags only. Today this affects only extending imagine, the closed loop and critic data to these tasks; plain runs call load_scene, which resets the attributes.
findings.evidence: Scratch probe /tmp/claude-1007/-home-michaellee-mclee-robocasa/13a5c8a4-4ec4-4d74-96b7-fb413333eea4/scratchpad/audit/stages-A/envattr.py on scene s0 of each task: load_scene, node = (state, py_state, capture), set the counters as a finished branch would leave them, then set_py_state + restore_node exactly as imagine/closedloop do. Results (logs envattr_*.log): RinseSinkBasin washed_loc stays [True, True, True]; WashLettuce washed_time stays 30; ScrubCuttingBoard timer stays 5 with 5 positions. In all three, _check_success() is True at the untouched scene start and the sim state equals the node bit for bit. py_state keys listed in the log are all fixtures, with no env attribute. grep finds no handling of washed_time, washed_loc or board_contact in any restore user.
findings.test: Run envattr.py (above). End-to-end version: from a WashLettuce decision point after the lettuce is under the stream, run two candidates with identical seeds through collect.decision_point or closedloop. Their sim states match, but the second candidate's success/steps differ (it starts with a larger washed_time).
findings.fix: Treat the task's own Python state as part of a node. In capture(obs=True) and py_state, add an '__env__' entry with the attributes the task class sets in _setup_scene, _reset_internal or update_state (washed_time; washed_loc; board_contact_positions (a list of np arrays, which _plain() currently rejects, so deep-copy it explicitly), board_contact_timer, sponge_contact_height; for the other areas StirVegetables.success_time and GetToastedBread.toaster_on). Restore it last in restore_node, after set_state's update_state. Add a pre-flight test per task: change the counters, restore, and assert that _check_success() and the counters equal the node's.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute the finding and could not. I re-read the code and reproduced the leak in all three tasks, building the counters from real saved episodes rather than setting them by hand.

Code path:
- `hidden_state.py:52-60` `py_state` copies only fixtures whose class overrides `update_state`.
- `capture`/`restore` (`hidden_state.py:80-118`) copy the warm start, ctrl, the clock, the observables, the fixture py-state and the robot controllers. Nothing on the env object itself is copied.
- `restore_node` (`atomic_eval.py:84-97`) calls `set_state` (`oracle.py:76-82`, which runs `env.update_state()`), sets the sim state again, then calls `hidden_state.restore`. No env attribute is touched.
- `rollout()` never calls `env.reset`.
- The official counters live on the env:
  - `WashLettuce.washed_time`: set in `_setup_scene` (`wash_lettuce.py:31-33`), incremented in `update_state` (`57-60`), read in `_check_success` (`62-63`).
  - `RinseSinkBasin.washed_loc`: set in `__init__` and `_reset_internal` (`rinse_sink_basin.py:16-19, 38-41`), written inside `_check_success` itself (`62-73`).
  - `ScrubCuttingBoard.board_contact_positions`, `board_contact_timer`, `sponge_contact_height`: set in `_setup_scene` (`scrub_cutting_board.py:39-43`), appended in `update_state` (`81-110`), read in `_check_success` (`112-124`).
- So nothing captures or restores them. The only thing that resets them is `load_scene` (`reset_to` → `reset()` → `_reset_internal`/`_setup_scene`), which is called once per episode or decision point, not once per branch.
- A grep over `runs/` finds `washed_time`, `washed_loc` and `board_contact` only in `stage_trace.py` (debug output) and a docstring in `atomic_steps_seen11.py:17-21`. That docstring already notes that this state is not in the MuJoCo state, but the restore modules never handle it.

Empirical check: my probe is `/tmp/claude-1007/-home-michaellee-mclee-robocasa/13a5c8a4-4ec4-4d74-96b7-fb413333eea4/scratchpad/audit/skeptic-stagesA-counters/probe.py`, with logs `probe_<task>.log` in the same folder. It runs CPU only. For each task it does load_scene, then builds node0 exactly as `closedloop.py:57` / `imagine.py:105` do. As the branch it replays the saved successful seen480 episode with `set_state` + `_check_success` at every step, which is what `env.step`'s `_post_action` plus the gym wrapper's `_check_success` do. Then it calls `set_py_state` + `restore_node(node0)` as `closedloop.py:66-67` does. Results:
- **WashLettuce s0:** the branch reaches `washed_time` 29 (official success at step 556). After restoring t=0 it is still 29. The sim state equals the node bit for bit, and `_check_success()` is True at the untouched scene start. One `env.step` then gives reward/success True.
- **RinseSinkBasin s11:** after restore, `washed_loc` is still `[True, True, True]` and the check is True at t=0.
- **ScrubCuttingBoard s0:** after restore, the timer is still 7 with 7 positions, and the check is True at t=0 (the gripper starts more than 15 cm from the sponge).
- **Restore increments the counter:** for a WashLettuce node captured with `capture(obs=True)` at t=532 (lettuce under the stream, `washed_time`=1), five consecutive `restore_node` calls give 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
- **Partial branches leak too:** after one 16-step candidate from that node, the next candidate starts with `washed_time` 23 instead of 1, two steps short of the 25 that success needs. A partial branch leaks as well as a finished one.

The sim-state guards (`collect.py:160-167`, `closedloop.py:80-82`, `restore_node`'s own equality check) pass, because the counters do not affect physics.

Corrections to the finding:
1. **Wrong line numbers** for two official files. `rinse_sink_basin.py:125-136` and `scrub_cutting_board.py:172-215` do not exist (the files have 73 and 124 lines). The correct ranges are given above. `wash_lettuce.py:57-63` is right.
2. **Where `washed_loc` is written.** `RinseSinkBasin.washed_loc` is changed inside `_check_success`, not `update_state`. So restoring does not increment it. It is changed by every `_check_success` call: the gym wrapper's step, our final stage check, `stage_trace`.
3. **`sponge_contact_height`** is set but never read. It is harmless and not needed for success.
4. **Leaks are not only finished branches.** Any partial progress leaks, and in the closed loop it compounds across the N candidates plus the executed chunk at every boundary.

Does it matter for results? No existing result is affected:
- Plain runs and atomic_eval call `load_scene` per job.
- imagine jobs cover only KettleBoiling, SteamInMicrowave and PackIdenticalLunches (`jobs_*.json`).
- Critic-data jobs cover only those 3 tasks.
- `closedloop.L_STAGE` has only those 3 tasks.
- Those 3 tasks have no env-level counters. I grepped all 16 task classes: only ScrubCuttingBoard, WashLettuce, RinseSinkBasin, StirVegetables (`success_time`) and GetToastedBread (`toaster_on`) keep such state.

It is a silent blocker for extending imagine, the closed loop, critic data, or any restore-based state-understanding work to these tasks. After the first successful branch, every later branch from an earlier node would count as an official success after one step, and nothing would fail.

I rate it major, not critical, because it is latent. Do fix it before any restore-based work on the 16 tasks.

Related, not verified here: atomic_eval's `reset_seed_*` with step>0 calls `load_scene` and then starts from a mid-episode state. That resets the counters to 0 rather than to the source episode's value at that point. So the fix should store the node's value, not zero it.

- `WashLettuce.washed_time`: set to 0 in `_setup_scene` (`wash_lettuce.py:31-33`), +1 per `update_state` while the lettuce is under water (`57-60`).
- `RinseSinkBasin.washed_loc`: reset in `__init__` and `_reset_internal` (`rinse_sink_basin.py:16-19, 38-41`), and set inside `_check_success` itself (`62-73`).

Every branch from a node (`imagine.candidate`, the closed loop's N candidates plus the executed chunk, `collect.py`'s N×M rollouts) starts with whatever the previous branch left. In addition, `oracle.set_state` (called by `restore_node` and by `imagine.restore`) runs `update_state`, so each restore of a node with the lettuce under the stream adds 1 to `washed_time`.

No existing result is affected. findings.title: SteamInMicrowave stages 1-2 never re-check vegetable_in_bowl (and stage 2 not bowl_in_microwave): dead-end stage finishes are credited
findings.where: runs/scripts/atomic_steps.py:97-103 (stage 1: bowl inside + gripper far; stage 2: door closed); runs/scripts/atomic_eval.py:152-157 (stages latched, earlier ones never re-checked); official steam_in_microwave.py:213-222
findings.description: The official success needs vegetable_in_bowl AND bowl_in_microwave AND door_closed AND turned_on at the same time. Stage 0 checks the vegetable once and is then latched. Stage 1 checks only the bowl and stage 2 only the door. A rollout whose vegetable falls out while the bowl is carried is still credited with stages 1 and 2. From that state the official success is unreachable unless the bowl comes back out. This is the same class of bug as the PackIdenticalLunches 'either tupperware' dead end, but it is not documented as such for SteamInMicrowave. It inflates 'reached', the stage-completion labels of the critic data (done = reached > k), the closed loop's 'finished' candidates and the V curves used to locate critical chunks. The labeler_check could not detect it because it ran only on successful demos.
findings.evidence: seen480 SteamInMicrowave s6: history [[304,0],[688,1],[800,2]], reached 3, failure. Probe sim_dead.py: at t=688 (stage 1 credited) and t=800 (stage 2 credited), veg_in_bowl=False, with the vegetable on the robot base at z=0.408. s28 (diagnosis _notes.md:36): the tomato rolled out at 662, stage 1 was credited at 816 and stage 2 at 1072, and START was pressed at 1177; only the spill cost the success. Critic data (data/SteamInMicrowave/*/results.jsonl): stage-1 finishes without success whose stage-0 check is False at the finish (prev_ok False, with the gripper >25 cm from the bowl, so the vegetable is not in it): coarse 144/1212 (11.9 %), dense 21/74 (28 %), confirm 4/22.
findings.test: For every critic-data rollout with k=1, done and not success: load roll/<tag>_t<t>_c<i>_m<m>.npz, set_state at the first boundary where stage 1 holds, and evaluate OU.check_obj_in_receptacle(env,'vegetable','bowl'). Then measure the final success rate reachable from those nodes, as was done for PIL in 20261029_closedloop.
findings.fix: Make each non-final stage check include the official conjuncts that later stages still need: stage 1 = veg_in_bowl and bowl inside and released; stage 2 = door_closed and veg_in_bowl and bowl inside. Generally, stage k should be the AND of stage k's own conjuncts and every earlier official conjunct the final check still reads. Re-derive the critic labels from the saved states (bounds or roll npz) instead of re-collecting, and re-validate the stage checks on failed seen480 rollouts, not only on successful demos.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute the finding and could not. I re-read the code and re-scored the saved states myself.

**Code**
- runs/scripts/atomic_steps.py:97-103:
  - stage 1 checks only `obj_inside_of(bowl, microwave)` and `gripper_obj_far(bowl)`;
  - stage 2 checks only `microwave.is_closed`.
- The official check needs all four conjuncts at once: vegetable_in_bowl, bowl_in_microwave, door_closed, turned_on. It is at robocasa/environments/kitchen/composite/steaming_food/steam_in_microwave.py:118-127. The 213-222 cited in the finding is wrong; the file has 127 lines.
- runs/scripts/atomic_eval.py:152-153 latches the stage index; earlier stages are never re-checked.
- Every "finished" label inherits this:
  - critic data: collect.py:165 `done = reached > k or success`;
  - 20261028_critical/data.py `outcomes()` uses `done` only;
  - closedloop.py and imagine.py use the same rule.
- `prev_ok` is logged but unused. The closedloop README (under "Fixed before the launch") says imagine stopped using it on 2026-10-30. The reason given was that the 25 cm gripper-release condition rejected about 20 % of the stage-2 finishers. Dropping it also dropped the vegetable-in-bowl requirement.

**seen480 episodes (official predicates on the saved states, CPU env without rendering)**
- s6: veg_in_bowl is True at t=400 and False from t=432 on, with the vegetable at z=0.408. Stage 1 is credited at 688 and stage 2 at 800.
- s28: the vegetable is out from t=672. Stage 1 is credited at 816 and stage 2 at 1072. At 1177-1400, bowl_in_mw, door_closed and turned_on are all True; only veg_in_bowl fails.
- Both episodes have reached=3 and fail. The diagnosis notes label them undid_previous_stage, but the online history and the report's stage view credit stages 1 and 2.

**Critic data: all 1,989 done rollouts with k=1 or 2, scored at their last saved state**

| k | dataset | dead ends / done | dead from the start point | new spills |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | coarse | 148 / 1212 | 75 | 73 (6 %) |
| 1 | dense | 21 / 74 | 15 | 6 |
| 1 | confirm | 4 / 22 | 0 | 4 |
| 2 | coarse | 17 / 451 | 15 | 2 |
| 2 | dense | 1 / 116 | 0 | 1 |
| 2 | confirm | 0 / 65 | 0 | 0 |

- "Dead from the start point" means the vegetable was already out of the bowl at the decision point. These come almost entirely from the s6, s28 and s16 main runs.
- In every dead end the vegetable is out of the bowl. The bowl was inside the microwave at every k=1 and k=2 finish, so the "stage 2 does not check bowl_in_microwave" half of the finding has no case in the data.
- At k=1, `prev_ok` is an accurate proxy: 142 of its 144 flags are confirmed, and it misses 6 dead ends where the recomputed contact flickers.
- At k=2, `prev_ok` is a poor proxy: 107 of its 122 flags are false alarms, caused by the gripper being within 25 cm of the bowl while closing the door.

**Why it matters**
1. **V curves are wrong for whole episodes.**
   - s28 stage 1: raw V 0.69 / 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00 at t=320-800, corrected 0.31 / 0.19 / 0 / 0. At the k=2 point t=960: raw 0.94, corrected 0.
   - s6 at t=320: raw 0.94, corrected 0.06. The outcome was already decided by the stage-0 placement (the wedge near the rim), which a per-stage V cannot see even after the fix.
   - The s16 stage-1 jump at t=960-976 in critical_chunks.json (0.12→0.56) is an artefact: the corrected V is 0 throughout. Dense data was collected there.
   - So vegetable spills, a real SteamInMicrowave failure mode, are invisible to the critical-chunk search and enter the critic labels as successes.
2. **The SteamInMicrowave confirmation shrinks.** With dead-end finishes scored as failures, the cross-validated pick gain drops from +20 to +6 points. The perfect best-of-8 gain drops from 29 to 24.
   - At s1 t624, the picked candidate c5 was credited a finish in continuation 1 that was a dead end (the vegetable ended 33 cm from the bowl), and its point gain falls from +0.81 to 0.
   - At s23 t688, 3 of 18 finishes have the vegetable on the floor.
   - The pooled "+25.3" over 32 points falls to about +22.6.
3. **Headline success numbers are not inflated.** The final stage is the official check, and the SteamInMicrowave closed loop got 10/10 anyway. Dead-end finishes can only steer search and closed loop into unwinnable states; they cannot fake a success.

Major is the right severity, because the learned critic and the state-understanding work will train on these labels.

verdict.corrected_description:
**The flaw.** SteamInMicrowave's stage checks never require the vegetable to stay in the bowl after stage 0:
- runs/scripts/atomic_steps.py:97-100: stage 1 checks only bowl in microwave and gripper far from the bowl.
- atomic_steps.py:101-103: stage 2 checks only the door closed.
- atomic_eval.py:152-153 latches stages, so earlier stages are never re-checked.

The official check (steam_in_microwave.py:118-127) needs vegetable_in_bowl at the end. A rollout that spills the vegetable while carrying the bowl is therefore credited with stages 1 and 2 although success is unreachable. `prev_ok` is logged in the critic data, but `data.outcomes`, imagine and closedloop all use `done` alone.

**Confirmed cases**
- seen480 s6: vegetable out from t=432, stages credited at 688 and 800.
- seen480 s28: vegetable out from t=672, stages credited at 816 and 1072. Door closed and START pressed, so only the spill failed the task.
- Critic data, k=1: 148/1212 coarse, 21/74 dense and 4/22 confirm finishes are dead ends. About half of the coarse ones start from points where the vegetable was already out (the s6, s28 and s16 main runs). New spills inside the rollout are 73/1212 (6 %) coarse.
- Critic data, k=2: 17/451 coarse dead ends, 15 of them already dead at the start point. The bowl never left the microwave at any finish, so the bowl_in_microwave half of the finding is theoretical.
- `prev_ok` is a good dead-end proxy at k=1 (142 of its 144 flags are real), but not at k=2 (107 of 122 are false alarms from the 25 cm gripper rule).

**Consequences**
- V curves are wrong for s28 (raw V about 1.0 vs corrected 0 at t≥640) and s6. The s16 stage-1 "jump" at t=960 is an artefact.
- The SteamInMicrowave confirmation shrinks from +20 to +6 points, mainly at s1 t624. The pooled +25.3 falls to about +22.6.
- Headline success rates (plain, imagine, closed loop 10/10) are not inflated.

**Fix**
- Make stage 1 require veg_in_bowl, and stage 2 require veg_in_bowl and bowl_in_mw. Carry only the official conjuncts forward, not the release conditions.
- Re-derive the labels from the saved roll states.
- Even with the fix, s6's spill was already decided at the stage-0 placement (corrected V_1 is 0.06 at t=320), which a per-stage V cannot see.

findings.title: StackBowlsCabinet stage list assumes one-by-one placement; the policy (21/21 successes) and the official class docstring nest the bowls on the counter first, so the stages collapse to a single real stage
findings.where: runs/scripts/atomic_steps.py:44-51 (_first_bowl_in), 84-92; official stack_bowls_cabinet.py:10-13 (docstring: stack then move), 79-95
findings.description: The stages come from the human annotation (PickPlaceCounterToCabinet x2). The official success does not require that order, and the official docstring describes nest-then-carry. The frozen policy always nests first. Stage 0 ('a bowl inside the cabinet, released') is then credited only when the nested pair lands in the cabinet, and stage 1 follows 1-4 chunks later, once the gripper has retreated 25 cm. The decisive sub-task, nesting on the counter (6 of the 9 failures), is invisible to the stage tracker. Any stage-level critical-chunk location, critic label or closed-loop budget for this task sees stage 0 as 'everything' and stage 1 as 'retreat'. Conversely, a stage-0 credit by a lone bowl (one-by-one fallback) is a practical dead end for this policy: 0/4 such episodes finished.
findings.evidence: seen480 histories: in all 21 successes the gap from stage 0 to stage 1 is 16-64 steps ([16 x6, 32 x10, 48 x3, 64 x2]). Diagnosis StackBowlsCabinet/_summary.md: 'All 21 successes used nest-then-carry'; 'Every episode that ended up one-by-one failed (0/4: s1, s5, s17, s20)'. Failures s1, s5 and s17 have stage 0 credited by a lone bowl.
findings.test: At each seen480 StackBowlsCabinet stage-0 credit boundary, evaluate OU.check_obj_in_receptacle both ways and obj_inside_of for both bowls. Expect both bowls nested and inside in every success, and a lone bowl in s1/s5/s17.
findings.fix: Before using StackBowlsCabinet for stage-level work, add an order-free intermediate stage 'nested (bowl1 in bowl2 or bowl2 in bowl1) and released, anywhere', or define stage 0 as 'nested OR one bowl in the cabinet', and keep the final stage as _check_success(). Confirm the decomposition with the user, since it departs from the annotation.

That is the official check at chunk ends only.

verdict.corrected_description:
Some of our stage checks hold only while their condition is true at that moment; they are not a record that the stage was done. These are the release/far clauses, held-now pick stages and the toaster state. Two consumers re-evaluate them after the stage was latched, and both report false regressions:
- `prev_ok` (collect.py:166, imagine.py:83)
- `stage_trace.analyze`'s `first_incomplete_stage` (stage_trace.py:353-371, which uses true_at_end, successes included)

**SearingMeat:**
- Stage 0 (atomic_steps_seen11.py:194) adds `gripper_obj_far(pan)`. That is not an official conjunct: the official check only needs `gripper_obj_far(meat)`.
- When the meat is released the gripper is 2.9-16.8 cm from the pan, so `prev_ok` is False at all 11 seen480 stage-1 completions.

- StirVegetables stage 2 (PickUpSpatula, held now) is blamed in 8 failures: s0, s6, s12, s13, s15, s17, s22, s24.

  - SteamInMicrowave `prev_ok` is False at 9 of 42 completions.
  - KettleBoiling s13 and PrepareCoffee s0 have the same release-clause problem.

**Impact:**
- No current result depends on these fields. `prev_ok` is logged only and nothing reads it. `first_incomplete_stage` only feeds the diagnosis packets, and the report uses the agents' `root_cause_stage`.
- The issue was already noted in seen480/diagnosis/_tooling_issues.md:51-53 and SearingMeat/_summary.md:15, but never fixed.

**Fix (before either field becomes a critic or state-understanding label):**
- Latch each stage after its first pass and recheck only its at-target part.
- Pick stages count as done once the next stage starts.
- Keep real undos such as dropped objects or food out of the bowl.

Because of this, the same scene with the same seed is not a reproducible unit. Every plain, imagine, closed-loop and critic re-run is a new draw. findings.evidence: (1) Critic data, settled-v5 rows with per-key fingerprints. All N x M rollouts of a point start from the same restored state, and the state keys never differed. StackBowlsCabinet_s13 is bit-identical over all 6 runs (88 chunks). (4) CPU segmentation survey of scenes s0-s4 at t0 (scratch survey/*.json): visible semi-transparent pixels per 256x256 camera. The window (window_group_room_mat2, alpha 0.14-0.7) covers up to about 18k px (27 % of the image) in PreSoakPan, RinseSinkBasin, WashLettuce, SetUpCuttingStation, ScrubCuttingBoard, LoadDishwasher and SteamInMicrowave, and up to 14k px in GetToastedBread. Microwave, stove and toaster-oven glass covers up to about 10k px in KettleBoiling and StirVegetables, and up to 7k px in SearingMeat, including the wrist camera. Fridge glass and drawers (alpha 0.44-0.7) cover up to 22k px in PackIdenticalLunches on all three cameras, including the wrist. Other tasks: DeliverStraw's target glass cup (alpha 0.2) up to 1.1k px, PrepareCoffee up to 3.9k, StoreLeftoversInBowl up to 850, StackBowlsCabinet up to 172. Exposure tracks the noise: wrist noise is 35 % on PackIdenticalLunches (fridge glass in view) and 0.7 % on KettleBoiling (none in view). (5) The opaque-glass diagnostic in render_probe.py only matches material names containing 'Clear'. It misses the window, fridge drawers, flames and water.
findings.test: GPU, about 10 min. Run render_probe.py with K=50 on 5 scenes x 16 tasks at t0, plus seen480 step states with a burner lit or water running. Run it solo and with 16 concurrent renderers, and record distinct images and varying pixels per geom. Repeat with (a) offsamples=0 and (b) every alpha<1 material and site made opaque, to confirm the cause per task.
findings.fix: Choose and document one rendering policy before collecting state-understanding data. Options, best first: (A) Record-and-replay of actions (no fidelity cost; see the record-and-replay finding). (B) Deterministic CPU rendering through Mesa llvmpipe: __EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES=/usr/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d/50_mesa.json with MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID=4 (it is index 8 when both EGL vendors are loaded). Measured here: 1 distinct image in 10 renders per camera on KB, SIM and PIL, and identical across processes and LP_NUM_THREADS=1 vs the default. Fidelity cost: compared with the saved NVIDIA policy images at 6 states, 45-92 % of pixels differ, mean 0.7-2.7 levels, 0.4-1.4 % of pixels by more than 8 levels. That is more than the GPU noise, so a paired success-rate check against GPU is required. Speed: 0.19-0.32 s per render on this loaded machine. Rendering only at chunk boundaries removes most of that cost: the policy reads only the last step's 3 images, yet the env renders all 3 cameras every step (48 per chunk). (C) A GPU render cache: memoize sim.render keyed by qpos, mocap, model.site_rgba / site_size (flames, water), geom_rgba, mat_rgba, camera and resolution. It keeps the official images and makes revisited states identical; about 52 KB per PNG, 155 KB per chunk boundary. findings.description: load_scene does not reset the controllers' cached kinematics left by the previous rollout in the same env. capture() right after load_scene therefore records stale values. The closedloop README calls the result (a state difference of about 1e-13) fine. Under identical recorded actions it grows to 0.02-0.18 within one stage. It also affects the critic t=0 rows, whose docstring claims the main run's exact hidden state. Their outcomes depend on worker count and job order. seen480 is not affected: with 32 workers and 30 jobs per task, every job got a fresh env. The closed loop is not affected either (one process per episode). t>0 critic points are not affected, because settle() overwrites the caches.

findings.title: Physics is reproducible only on CPUs that select the same OpenBLAS kernel
findings.where: envs/groot numpy 2.2.5 with scipy-openblas 0.3.28 DYNAMIC_ARCH; robosuite OSC linear algebra; runs/README.md:78 ('Physics: bitwise identical')
findings.description: The claim that physics is bitwise identical given the same state and actions holds on this CPU (Xeon Silver 4210R, AVX-512, OpenBLAS SkylakeX kernel). OpenBLAS picks its kernel at runtime from the CPU. A different kernel changes controller results in the last bits from the first step, and the trajectory then drifts by about 0.4 within one stage. On another server, recorded-action replays, frozen-scene re-runs and the restore pre-flights will not match this machine's data. The hand-off README describes exactly such a server move.
findings.evidence: Same recorded actions for KettleBoiling s0 t0 (stage 0, 368 steps). The default run and the run with NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES='AVX512F AVX512CD AVX512_SKX AVX512_CLX' match the saved GPU-machine run bitwise. With OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Haswell it differs from step 1 (2.9e-13): 0.079 at step 256, 0.38 at step 368. The rendered images were identical across all three settings.
findings.test: On the target machine, replay 10 recorded decision points per task and compare states bitwise with this machine's. As a local proxy, repeat with OPENBLAS_CORETYPE in {Haswell, Zen, SkylakeX}.
findings.fix: Set OPENBLAS_CORETYPE explicitly in every launcher, and write it, the CPU model and numpy's show_config into each result row. Keeping SkylakeX keeps the existing data exact but requires an AVX-512 CPU. Switching to Haswell is portable to any AVX2 CPU but needs a new baseline.

findings.title: Executed actions are never saved, so committed paths cannot be replayed and restores at t>0 have to be inferred
findings.where: runs/20261029_closedloop/closedloop.py:85-99; runs/20261026_imagine/imagine.py (result rows keep only path = [stage, candidate]); runs/scripts/atomic_eval.py:259-269 (baseline saves step states and digest fingerprints, not actions); runs/20261029_closedloop/replay.py
findings.description: The closed loop executes recorded chunks, and imagine commits exact end states, but neither saves the actions. Reproducing an episode therefore means asking the policy again, which diverges on render noise: replay.py failed on all 5 PackIdenticalLunches replays, and the KettleBoiling replays drifted. The seen480 main runs save per-step states but not actions. Every critic decision point at t>0 therefore needs the inferred settle() hidden state, which is where restore bugs 4 and 5 came from. Physics alone is exactly replayable, so storing the actions would make every executed path exactly reproducible and would give exact hidden states at any t.
findings.evidence: replay_check / replay_fast2 (scratch fast/*.jsonl). The recorded actions of saved critic rollouts were re-executed in a new process, with CPU rendering and dummy images after the first request. The states were bitwise equal to the saved GPU-run states at every step: KB s0 t400 (16+16 steps), KB s14 t160 (208+176), PIL s10 t320 (80+80), SIM s12 t160 (432+432), SIM s13 t320 (512+496), and KB s0 t0 (368). The state keys of the first request were equal as well.
findings.test: After adding action logging, replay each closed-loop out/<tag>.json from load_scene with the stored actions. Require bitwise-equal states at every node, and the same stage changes and success.
findings.fix: Store each chunk's executed actions (16 x 12 float32), its seed and the request fingerprint. In closedloop log, save cands[pick]['chunk']; in imagine, the chunks of the committed path; in the baseline, an actions.npz next to _steps.npz. For new main runs, derive hidden states by re-executing the stored actions from load_scene instead of using settle().

findings.title: The EGL device index equals the GPU only because launchers set PCI order; one launcher does not

findings.title: Task-level accumulators and latches (env attributes) are never captured or restored, so they leak between rollouts and are lost across envs
findings.where: runs/scripts/hidden_state.py:52-60 (py_state iterates only kenv.fixtures), :80-95 (capture), :98-118 (restore); runs/scripts/atomic_eval.py:84-97 (restore_node); consumers runs/20261029_closedloop/closedloop.py:57,66,77,88, runs/20261026_imagine/imagine.py:32-35,75,86, runs/20261026_critic_data/collect.py:141,155. findings.description: Five of the 16 official success checks read counters or latches stored on the task env instance itself, not on a fixture. update_state() or _check_success() mutate them on every step. py_state()/set_py_state() only walk kenv.fixtures, and capture()/restore() only cover the robots, observables and timestep/cur_time, so no restore path saves or restores these attributes. Two consequences follow. (a) Each rollout from a node inherits whatever the previous rollout (candidate) left: washing, stirring, scrubbing and spout positions add up across candidates, and toaster_on stays latched. Later candidates and the committed chunk then get stage-done and official success they did not earn. (b) Restoring a node in another env, or after load_scene, loses the node's value. On top of that, restore_node's set_state() re-runs kenv.update_state(), which adds one more increment per restore, and only fixture state is undone afterwards. Every existing guard compares sim state only (restore_node's array_equal, closedloop's 'exact', collect's states[0] and first-chunk equality, preflight's restore_ps, which covers fixtures only), so the leak is silent. So far only KettleBoiling, SteamInMicrowave and PackIdenticalLunches have used restore, and none of them has task-level state, so existing results are not affected. findings.evidence: Scratch scripts are in /tmp/claude-1007/-home-michaellee-mclee-robocasa/13a5c8a4-4ec4-4d74-96b7-fb413333eea4/scratchpad/audit/restore-fixtures/. enumerate_state.py (one baseline episode per task, replayed with set_state + _check_success, plus 40 live steps; diff of every plain attribute of env, fixtures and objects): across all 16 tasks the only env attributes that change, apart from timestep/cur_time, are washed_time, success_time, prev_obj_pos_veg1/2, board_contact_positions/timer and washed_loc, and none of them is in py_state or capture. leak_test.py reproduces the closedloop.py node protocol (node = state + py_state + capture(obs=True); restore = set_py_state + restore_node), plays the rest of the episode as a stand-in candidate, then restores. Results: WashLettuce_s25 node t=464 has washed_time 2, the end has 34, and three restores give 35, 36, 37, with _check_success() True at the node. StirVegetables_s21 node t=912: success_time 0, restored 5, success True. RinseSinkBasin_s9 t=224: washed_loc [F,T,F], restored [T,T,T], success True. ScrubCuttingBoard_s23 t=192: timer 1, restored 8. GetToastedBread_s1 t=160 (leak_test2.py): toaster_on False, restored True. Restoring in a fresh env: WashLettuce 1 instead of 2, Rinse [F,F,F] instead of [F,T,F], GTB (t=192) toaster_on False instead of True. Control: SteamInMicrowave microwave._turned_on is restored correctly (False). nonobs.py (collect.py's path): WashLettuce_s25 t=480, three rollouts of one decision point start with washed_time 19, 20, 21.

Either use an explicit whitelist {WashLettuce:[washed_time], StirVegetables:[success_time, prev_obj_pos_veg1, prev_obj_pos_veg2], ScrubCuttingBoard:[board_contact_positions, board_contact_timer, sponge_contact_height], RinseSinkBasin:[washed_loc], GetToastedBread:[toaster_on]}, or take all plain/ndarray attributes of vars(kenv) minus a static skip list. In both cases add a guard test like enumerate_state.py that fails when any env attribute outside the list changes during an episode. Put it in py_state (so ps, imagine.restore, collect and preflight's diffs carry it) and in every capture, with or without obs. Restore it AFTER set_state in restore_node for every restore, not only obs nodes. Record attributes absent at capture time and delattr them on restore (prev_obj_pos_* is created lazily).
